item.title: Kotohiragu Shrine: The 785-Step Climb — Guide
item.description: Kotohiragu, affectionately known as Konpira-san, is one of Japan’s most beloved shrines, dedicated to the guardian deity of seafarers and long a pilgrimage destination drawing visitors from across the country. It sits high on the wooded slopes of Mount Zozu above the town of Kotohira, and reaching it is famously a climb: a stone stairway of 785 steps to the main shrine, or 1,368 all the way to the inner shrine.

item.title: Ikaho Onsen: A Historic Stone-Step Hot Spring Town — Guide
item.description: Ikaho Onsen’s most distinctive feature is its main street — a flight of 365 stone steps, one for each day of the year, lined with ryokan, shops and shrines climbing up the hillside, said to represent life’s journey. The town’s hot spring water, tinged a striking rust-orange from its high iron content and known as ‘golden water’ (kogane no yu), contrasts with the clear ‘silver water’ (shirogane no yu) also found here, and each September the town celebrates its heritage with a lively Stone Steps Festival featuring traditional performances along the steps.
